body:
**Regarding first issue:** This goes in one with the third issue you are talking about. So, you tell in the third issue, that there is a "bad user experience". But the first issue states the complete opposite (as far as I understand your issues). If you are explicitly navigating to the "/en" route, I – as a user – don't want to be redirected to the "de" route. Instead, it would be nice by *you* to create something like a banner, and tell the user "Hey, we saw that you are german, would you like to view the page in german".

> apple.com has a client-side detection which then shows a message asking if you want to change to a different locale. If there's enough interest in this type of solution we can provide tools for this approach as well.

– Quote from [I18n RFC](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/17078)

**Regarding second issue:** I *suppose* (as far as I can read from the [official specs](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7231#section-5.3.5) – since Next.js is using the [`@hapi/accept` package](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/788183e8d3c6e354e24a89febcfdc482fc55640b/packages/next/next-server/server/next-server.ts#L335) for leveraging the `Accept-Language` header) that this is indeed the right behavior. However, I am completely with you, that this should not be the case.
I don't know completely how the browsers treat the headers explicitly, but normally browsers like Chrome and Firefox should also send the "de" flag as a lower quality to the user agent. So it would look somehow like this:

```
de-AT,de;q=0.9,en-US;q=0.8,en;q=0.8
```

**Regarding your third issue:** Indeed [there is a cookie, that should be set](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/788183e8d3c6e354e24a89febcfdc482fc55640b/packages/next/next-server/server/next-server.ts#L419), when the user visits a locale specifically. However, I am also not able to make it work for me on my application.

Added with Edit 2: The cookie cannot properly work (or at least, is only working for custom domains for each locale right now), because [this commit](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/2ab34451b7f36745f33a69fb35256f40fd13eac1#diff-bd7baf53ff559d84461af8b2fd62cade7e2d8eb203f489e24a27c5b83a79a9d3L367) just ticked the variable which causes the cookie to be set to "false"

---

**Edit 1:** Add a reference to `@hapi/accept` package.

**Edit 2:** Add reference why cookie is not working to third issue.

because they all serve the same language version.

**Regarding second issue:** hmm, not sure then, to be honest. I just set the browser language to "de-at" in FF and it did not work, only when I added "de" as well.

**Regarding third issue:** I think I'll just set **localeDetection** to false for now, and simply show a banner to the user notifying them that they can browse the site in a different locale, providing them a link.

issue.title: Accept-Language (i18n) header not evaluated when directly accessing sub-routes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Issue was opened via the bug report template.

issue.title: Accept.language does not match more specific language tag
issue.body:
Hi there :wave: 

@dotkuro and I have noticed a small bug in the code responsible for matching preferences to accepted values.
While developing a web application, we noticed that when we provide content in `de-DE` and the browser requests just `de`, `accept.language` does not match any language tag. This affects NextJS downstream, [where we first encountered this issue](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/20488#issuecomment-770890446).

According to [RFC 4647](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4647#section-3.3.1), a language range (i.e. `de`) should match a language tag (i.e. `de-DE`), if it is a prefix of the tag and not just an exact match:

> A language range matches a particular language tag if, in a case-insensitive comparison, it exactly equals the tag, or if it exactly equals a prefix of the tag such that the first character following the prefix is "-". 

We believe we have identified the piece of code responsible for this behavior:
https://github.com/hapijs/accept/blob/f3737593e0b6455057a0698ec9bbafb1063aa0d2/lib/header.js#L194

Here, only exact matches from our preferences are considered.

body: There's now a PR in https://github.com/hapijs/accept/pull/64 which fixes matching of a more specific language tag if a less specific one is requested :tada:

The Problem is now fixed in `@hapi/accept v5.0.2`. Updating the dependency should fix the faulty detection, when only requesting a prefix. i.e: When requesting `de` your page will now also ship `de-de`.

> next v10.2.0 still "@hapi/accept": "5.0.1", 😊 [6b97bce#diff-9c1a3867443c54525b4f24ef171f231a6e8bb065ffc8b7b62c4843d5ff62dd42L66](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/commit/6b97bcea5ba851740404e8192fc9ebff711e1b83#diff-9c1a3867443c54525b4f24ef171f231a6e8bb065ffc8b7b62c4843d5ff62dd42L66)

Feel free to open a PR

issue.title: Next.js 10 localization in pathname

repository.name: serverless-next.js
repository.description: ⚡ Deploy your Next.js apps on AWS Lambda@Edge via Serverless Components

issue.body:
The new built-in localization in Next.js 10 allows to have the locale as a path prefix, e.g.:

```
/about
/de/about
/es/about
```

All three routes will open `pages/about.tsx`. This works fine when I run it locally.
When I deploy it using serverless-next.js, it gives a 404 for `/de/about` and `/es/about`. Just `/about` still works.

Is this something that the Serverless Next.js Component doesn't support yet, or am I doing something wrong?
Thanks!

body:
@timneutkens there seem to be two PRs already created for this: https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/24283 and https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/23142

I can open a new one if these are outdated.
